label: Albums
description: 80 records — from the untouchable canon to the punchlines.

items.name: The Beatles — Abbey Road
items.note: The one with the crosswalk everyone still stops traffic for.

items.name: Michael Jackson — Thriller
items.note: Best-selling album of all time. Not close.

items.name: Pink Floyd — The Dark Side of the Moon
Fleetwood Mac — Rumours
items.note: A band falling apart made the best breakup album ever.

items.name: Lauryn Hill — The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
Kendrick Lamar — To Pimp a Butterfly
Stevie Wonder — Songs in the Key of Life
The Rolling Stones — Exile on Main St.
Kanye West — My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
Led Zeppelin — Led Zeppelin IV
items.note: Contains that song your local bar has banned on the guitar.

items.name: Miles Davis — Kind of Blue
items.note: The jazz album owned by people who don't own jazz albums.

items.name: Radiohead — In Rainbows
items.note: The pay-what-you-want one that was actually great.

items.name: Kendrick Lamar — good kid, m.A.A.d city
Wu-Tang Clan — Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
A Tribe Called Quest — The Low End Theory
The White Stripes — Elephant
items.note: Home of the riff every stadium plays.

items.name: Vampire Weekend — Modern Vampires of the City
Solange — A Seat at the Table
Bon Iver — For Emma, Forever Ago
items.note: Recorded alone in a cabin, as the legend contractually requires.

items.name: Kanye West — Yeezus
items.note: Abrasive on purpose. You've picked a side already.

items.name: Radiohead — Kid A
items.note: The 'they abandoned guitars' album.

items.name: Lou Reed — Metal Machine Music
items.note: An hour of feedback. Sold as an album. On purpose.

items.name: Sufjan Stevens — Carrie & Lowell
items.note: Devastating. Also a great way to end a party.

items.name: Swans — To Be Kind
items.note: Two hours long. Feels like four. That's the point.

items.name: The Velvet Underground & Nico
items.note: Sold few copies; everyone who bought one started a band.

items.name: Captain Beefheart — Trout Mask Replica
items.note: Genius or noise. There is no in-between camp.

items.name: Tool — Lateralus
items.note: The Fibonacci sequence, but make it a mosh pit.

items.name: Joanna Newsom — Ys
items.note: Five songs, a harp, and a voice you'll argue about.

items.name: Godspeed You! Black Emperor — Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven
Fiona Apple — Fetch the Bolt Cutters
items.note: The pandemic's most critically-adored, least hummable record.

items.name: My Chemical Romance — The Black Parade
items.note: An entire personality type in album form.

items.name: 100 gecs — 1000 gecs
items.note: Sounds like a Nintendo having a breakdown. Beloved anyway.

items.name: Kid Cudi — Man on the Moon: The End of Day
Lou Reed & Metallica — Lulu
items.note: I AM THE TABLE.

items.name: Kevin Federline — Playing with Fire
items.note: Mr. Britney Spears makes a rap album. It goes poorly.

items.name: Vanilla Ice — To the Extreme
items.note: Ice ice baby. That's the whole review.

items.name: Limp Bizkit — Chocolate Starfish and the Hot Dog Flavored Water
items.note: The title alone is a Tier-4 pick.

items.name: Creed — Human Clay
items.note: Sold 20 million copies. Everyone denies owning it.

items.name: Nickelback — All the Right Reasons
items.note: The internet's designated worst band, wildly successful.

items.name: Garth Brooks — ...In the Life of Chris Gaines
items.note: A country legend invents a goth rock alter-ego. Nobody asked.

items.name: Insane Clown Posse — The Great Milenko
items.note: Miracles. How do they work.

items.name: Paris Hilton — Paris
items.note: 'Stars Are Blind' is unironically fine, which nobody expected.

items.name: Soulja Boy — souljaboytellem.com
items.note: Youuu! (Crank that.)

items.name: William Shatner — The Transformed Man
items.note: Captain Kirk. Dramatically reciting. Rocket Man. Enough said.

items.name: Guns N' Roses — Chinese Democracy
items.note: Fourteen years and a reported $13 million in the making.
